messages:
aisha_cs: FYI customer AtlasAI reporting duplicate tokens and partial outputs after a reconnect. They say reconnect+resume sometimes appends the tail twice and they got charged twice. Repro steps and sample SSE below. Can infra/runtime triage? :eyes:

sam_customer: repro steps I used (short):
1) open SSE /v1/streams with idempotency token X
2) force TCP drop after ~1.2s of streaming (mid-response)
3) reconnect with resume_token from last event header
4) server resumes and the last ~30 tokens are re-emitted, but client also replays them locally — final output duplicates

sam_customer: sample raw events we captured:

-- initial connection --
event: chunk
data: {"seq": 0, "text": "The quick brown \""}

event: chunk
data: {"seq": 1, "text": "fox jumps over"}

--- connection dropped ---

-- reconnect --
event: resume_ack
data: {"resume_token": "rt_abc123", "next_seq": 2}

event: chunk
data: {"seq": 2, "text": " the lazy dog"}
event: done
data: [DONE]

sam_customer: client shows final concatenation: \"The quick brown \"fox jumps over the lazy dogthe lazy dog\" — duplicate tail

morgan_infra: thanks — couple quick q's: which SDK/language? and do they use auto-append on reconnect (client blindly replays unacked buffer)?

sam_customer: Node SDK, custom client they wrote. They keep unacked buffer and append incoming chunks on resume; so it looks like both sides are replaying. But billing shows 2x token count on our side for that request idempotency token (so we also charged twice sometimes).

ben_runtime: that last part worries me — are they reusing the same idempotency token across reconnects? They should, but our billing dedupe plane should catch duplicates based on request_id + resume markers. Need logs.

sam_customer: they reused token X for reconnect. I'll paste logs from our stream proxy (redacted):

[proxy] 2026-03-12T14:12:01Z accepted conn id=conn-9 token=X
[proxy] 2026-03-12T14:12:02Z stream chunk seq=0 size=12 -> sent to runtime node r-3
[proxy] 2026-03-12T14:12:03Z connection reset by peer
[proxy] 2026-03-12T14:12:03Z reconnect attempt with resume_token=rt_abc123
[runtime r-3] 2026-03-12T14:12:03Z resume request for token rt_abc123 last_ack_seq=1
[runtime r-3] 2026-03-12T14:12:03Z resumed at seq=2, re-emitting seq=2..4
[billing] 2026-03-12T14:12:04Z charge request tokens=45 req_id=X
[billing] 2026-03-12T14:12:04Z charge request tokens=32 req_id=X

ben_runtime: from that trace, runtime emitted resumed chunks and billing got two charges for same req_id. Could be double-emit at runtime or duplicate billing requests from proxy after reconnect. I need a deterministic repro with curl to test our resume codepath.

morgan_infra: @ben_runtime I can spin up a local env and run a flaky TCP proxy to simulate mid-response drop. If runtime re-emits on resume but we also replay buffered unacked at proxy, we'll double-send. We should assert that on reconnect the proxy only sends an explicit resume handshake and doesn't re-post previously-acked chunks.

ben_runtime: good plan. Also check resume semantics: our runtime marks resumed emissions as "replayed" vs "new" in the metrics. If billing service uses only seq ranges without the replay flag, duplicate charge can happen. I'll add an immediate metric check.

oncall_engr: tagging oncall since customer in prod and billing involved. @oncall_engr can you take over if infra needs infra-level packet capture?

devdeploy_bot: deploy started: resume-fix-experiment branch -> staging (job 4532)

aisha_cs: next steps for CS: I've asked AtlasAI to pause traffic for that idempotency token and given them a temporary credit while we investigate. They want ETA for root cause. Please advise if we should rollback staging change if it looks risky.

ben_runtime: quick hypothesis list: 
- proxy/client double-replay due to unacked buffer + resume handshake (most likely)
- runtime emitted duplicates because resume window logic allowed re-send of seq that were already delivered (edge case when last_ack_seq was stale)
- billing dedupe race where two billing requests accepted before dedupe cache populated

ben_runtime: repro plan I'm running now:
1) start local runtime with debug mode (seq logging)
2) run a flaky-proxy script that kills TCP after N ms
3) reconnect with same idempotency token and resume_token
4) assert runtime logs: only one billing call per req_id and resumed seq strictly > last_ack_seq

morgan_infra: I pushed flaky-proxy script to my laptop, command below to reproduce quickly:

# simulate drop after 800ms
node tools/flaky-proxy.js --target localhost:8080 --drop-after-ms 800 --listen 127.0.0.1:9000

# then curl from client to proxy
curl -N -H "Idempotency: X" http://127.0.0.1:9000/v1/streams

morgan_infra: initial results: runtime logs show resumed seq=2 and re-emit of seq 2..4, proxy also attempted to re-send buffered seq=2..4 on reconnect. So duplicate forward to runtime observed. Seems proxy logic needs to either acknowledge server resume or drop local replay if server confirms resume_ack.

ben_runtime: thanks. Short-term mitigation: runtime can include a resume_ack that contains last_seen_client_seq. If resume_ack.seq > client_unacked_start then client drop its local replay. But that's a protocol change; we can patch proxy to wait for resume_ack before replaying buffered data.

morgan_infra: agreed. I'll push a quick proxy change to wait for resume_ack and gate replay on it. That should reduce duplicates immediately. Will run a canary in staging.

aisha_cs: ETA to canary? customer wants update in 1-2 hours.

morgan_infra: canary in ~45m, monitoring for duplicate billing and double-emitted seqs. I'll post results here.

ben_runtime: I'll also add a short-term dedupe guard in billing: if we see two charge requests with same req_id within 5s, treat second as potential duplicate and hold for reconciliation. Not permanent but reduces impact while fix rolls.

sam_customer: thanks everyone. If you need the AtlasAI account logs I can DM them to the eng channel. They've enabled debug on their client and can help with packet traces.

morgan_infra: canary is up. Initial verdict: reduced duplicate forwards by ~95% in our tests. Billing spike suppressed by billing guard. I'll schedule staging -> prod rollout after 2h bake if no regressions.

aisha_cs: perfect. I'll tell AtlasAI we have a mitigation and will roll to prod if canary holds. Thanks all. :pray:
